Holcim Liban SAL Insolvency Disrupts Lebanon's Construction Materials Sector

BEIRUT, June 13—Holcim Liban SAL, one of Lebanon’s leading construction materials producers, has entered insolvency proceedings, sending ripples through the country’s building sector and raising fresh concerns about the stability of local supply chains.

The company, which has operated for decades as a key supplier of cement and related materials, confirmed its entry into insolvency late Wednesday. “In light of ongoing financial constraints and market disruptions, Holcim Liban SAL has initiated insolvency procedures. We are working closely with the court-appointed administrator to assess options for our operations and workforce,” a company spokesperson said in a statement.

Production at Holcim Liban’s main plant in Chekka has slowed significantly, according to several employees, some of whom have been temporarily laid off. “We have had to scale back shifts as orders have dried up and suppliers are demanding immediate payment,” said a maintenance supervisor who declined to be named.

Industry analysts say the insolvency is likely to exacerbate Lebanon’s ongoing construction slowdown, which has been aggravated by the country’s broader economic crisis. “Holcim Liban’s troubles will only deepen the shortage of locally produced cement, potentially raising prices and forcing builders to turn to more expensive imports,” said Rami Mhanna, a construction sector analyst at the Beirut Institute for Economic Studies.

The Lebanese Construction Workers Union called the situation “deeply worrying,” warning of potential job losses for hundreds of employees and contractors. “Workers are anxious about their future. We urge the authorities to ensure that workers’ rights are protected as the process unfolds,” said union leader Fadi Khoury.

Local trade groups such as the Building Materials Association have called for urgent government intervention to stabilize the sector, warning that delays in infrastructure and housing projects could follow.

As the insolvency proceedings continue, Holcim Liban SAL’s management said it remains committed to “transparent communication with stakeholders” while seeking a path forward for the company’s assets and employees.
